formattedAddress: No. 22之2號, Lane 38, Section 3, Zhinan Rd, Zhinan Village, Wenshan District, Taipei City, Taiwan 116

text.text:
Nice little hideaway on the top of the mountain with a nice view of Taipei 101 in the distant. The decor is well presented and the piped music of Christmas classics made you feel like you are not in Taipei but a Western country. The air is fresh but unfortunately the let down is that there is quite a fair amount of houseflies around on the table and food area, which dampens the dining experience.

The good is pretty decent, including the fried rice, fried tofu, fried mushrooms and french fries. The service could be better as there is little communication.

text.text: Second time here. Ordered 茶香豆腐and 铁观音茶鸡汤. One tip is to turn the soup stove to low heat and slowly let it simmer for 20-30min till the soup turn dark brown. That’s when the tea flavour is already infused. No high heat! No need to top up the soup as all the flavours would already be infused in the first round. This is a family restaurant, and the service personnel tried to be as helpful as much as they can. Not sure what kind of services people are expecting as mentioned in their reviews. 茶叶炒饭 also have some subtle tea flavour! Finished up the meal with their tie guan yin tea! 👍 Also ordered the local tea flavoured craft beers to try! If you know what to pick, all the dishes actually complement each other!

text.text: Tea infused fried rice is very tasty. Tea infused mee sua is a little heavy on the tea side. Rest of it was alright. Service is almost non existent and they only take cash.

The highlight was the exceptional hospitality of Eddie Pong, who not only served us with grace but also shared his passion for Taiwanese cuisine.
